pr_title: Avoid divide by zero errors in tplink light integration
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Some bulbs such as kl125 don't have a definition submitted into
pyHS100.  Trying to interact with them will cause a divide by
zero error:
```
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tplink/light.py", line 248, in attempt_update
    self._light_features = self._get_light_features()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tplink/light.py", line 289, in _get_light_features
    min_mireds = kelvin_to_mired(min_range)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/util/color.py", line 515, in color_temperature_kelvin_to_mired
    return math.floor(1000000 / kelvin_temperature)
ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
```

As the `pyHS100` project has been abandoned in favor of `python-kasa` but there isn't yet
a component in home assistant for using `python-kasa` add some fallback code into the component.

If the light specifies it supports color temperature but the range isn't available choose a "safe"
range that is the minimum of what is available in bulbs today.

issue_context.title: tplink: Error on device update! (division by zero)
issue_context.body:
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
I am trying to use my TP-Link lights with Home Assistant. I have the following on my local network:
* HS200 x 3
* HS220 x 1
* KL430 (not supported, I know)

Only the HS200 and HS220 lights are being registered, which is okay for this issue. The problem is a division by zero error from the tplink component.


## Environment

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 2021.1.5
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): unknown
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): raspberry pi running ubuntu 20.10
- Integration causing this issue: tplink
- Link to integration documentation on our website: [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tplink/](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tplink/)

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
This is occurring on a totally fresh install of home assistant with no configuration yaml


## Traceback/Error logs

```txt
Logger: homeassistant.components.light
Source: util/color.py:515
Integration: Light (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 4:02:02 PM (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 4:02:02 PM

tplink: Error on device update!
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 359, in _async_add_entity
    await entity.async_device_update(warning=False)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 466, in async_device_update
    await task
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tplink/light.py", line 468, in async_update
    is_ready = await self.hass.async_add_executor_job(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 57, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tplink/light.py", line 248, in attempt_update
    self._light_features = self._get_light_features()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tplink/light.py", line 289, in _get_light_features
    min_mireds = kelvin_to_mired(min_range)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/util/color.py", line 515, in color_temperature_kelvin_to_mired
    return math.floor(1000000 / kelvin_temperature)
ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
```

## Additional information
This appears to be caused when tplink attempts to convert kelvin values (min and max) into mired values. The homeassistant/util/color.py method `color_temperature_kelvin_to_mired` receives a value of 0 for the `kelvin_temperature` parameter from the tplink component and will throw the error.

The relevant piece of code at line 515 of color.py is:
```python
def color_temperature_kelvin_to_mired(kelvin_temperature: float) -> float:
    """Convert degrees kelvin to mired shift."""
    return math.floor(1000000 / kelvin_temperature)
```
comments:
Hey there @rytilahti, @thegardenmonkey, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`tplink`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L478) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
This is happening over and over for me with my 2 new KL125 bulbs. Neither have successfully integrated into my Kasa integration 😞

So the problem for KL430 and KL125 is the missing definition for color temperature ranges inside pyhs100. I'm not sure what's the simplest solution here until the integration gets ported to use python-kasa.

The simplest approach would be simply having a fallback default range inside homeassistant, 2700-5000 (or even 6500, if ignoring the KL120 US) would be supported by all bulbs listed at https://github.com/python-kasa/python-kasa/blob/master/kasa/smartbulb.py#L12

> This is happening over and over for me with my 2 new KL125 bulbs. Neither have successfully integrated into my Kasa integration 😞

What I did to fix mine was to edit smartbulb.py and add the temperature definition for KL125.  After restarting HA, it works.  I run in a docker container, so I copied the file outside of the container and then created a binding to ensure that I'm always using my copy of that file.

```
TPLINK_KELVIN = {'LB130': (2500, 9000),
                 'LB120': (2700, 6500),
                 'LB230': (2500, 9000),
                 'KB130': (2500, 9000),
                 'KL130': (2500, 9000),
                 'KL125': (2700, 6500),
                 'KL120': (2700, 6500)}
```

Perfect. Thanks!

review_comments:
`_get_valid_temperature_range` is called by `_get_light_features` which is called by `attempt_update` which is called by `async_update`.

Meaning this is constantly redetermined each time the light updates its state? Should this be determined once?
I don't believe that's correct.  It will only set the features the first time.  See https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/tplink/light.py#L249
